Redwood SE: draft reference architecture diagram and security callouts - Ethan to deliver by 2027-02-21
AstraCloud: provide VPC peering CIDR and staging account for test listing - Lina to provide by 2027-02-18
action_items: Ethan Cole: produce reference architecture draft by 2027-02-21

summary: Technical sync to align on marketplace listing process, joint reference architecture for Redwood private & dedicated deployments on AstraCloud marketplace, security controls (KMS, SOC2, SSO), and next steps to run a staging benchmark and produce listing assets.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Jensen (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Redwood Solutions); Samir Rao (AstraCloud), Lina Gomez (Cloud Architect), Vikram Singh (Security Lead), Ana Torres (Product)

[00:00] Maya Jensen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, happy Valentine's day, um and uh let's get started. we wanted to walk through the marketplace listing process and the joint reference architecture for Redwood running on AstraCloud. quick intros, then we'll go into the integration bits.

[00:22] Samir Rao: Thanks Maya, Samir here, i'll keep this high level from our side and Lina will walk through the networking bits.

[00:30] Lina Gomez: hi all, Lina. we'll be the engineering point, i have the staging env ready-ish, couple of things to confirm.

[01:05] Ethan Cole: awesome. quick agenda: 1) marketplace listing checklist and assets 2) reference architecture (hosted, dedicate, private) 3) security requirements (KMS, audit logs, SSO) 4) staging benchmark plan and next steps. sound good?

[01:28] Ana Torres: yes that works.

[02:05] Maya Jensen: ok first, listing assets. we need short/long descriptions, pricing tiers, logos, screenshots, and a reference architecture diagram. redwood has a marketplace checklist (link: https://redwood.ai/marketplace-checklist) — i'll share. sometimes the marketplace team asks for a 3rd party security attestation like SOC2 type 2, which we have, but you may want to include your marketplace onboarding security questionnaire.

[02:48] Vikram Singh: on SOC2 — we run internal procurement checks, we'll need the SOC2 report and also a section on data residency and logs. can you confirm where logs live for hosted vs dedicated vs private?

[03:15] Ethan Cole: yes — hosted API stores logs in redwood-managed logs with retention policies; dedicated keeps tenant logs in isolated S3 buckets we can configure to ship to your account or to a retention policy; private (VPC/on-prem) keeps everything in your environment, logs remain in your storage. note: transcription may show Redwood 'dedicate' occasionally in docs — sorry the auto transcript there.

[04:00] Lina Gomez: good. for marketplace listing we also need a reference architecture that shows VPC peering, optional private control plane, and how billing flows. how does the billing integration work with AWS/Astra marketplace?

[04:28] Maya Jensen: generally there are two models: 1) marketplace-managed billing (customers purchase via your marketplace, we consume metering reports for usage reconciliation) or 2) bring-your-own-billing where customer bills directly and marketplace is just a discovery channel. we'll coordinate with your marketplace ops to confirm procurement flow.

[05:05] Samir Rao: AstraCloud Marketplace prefers the marketplace-managed billing for SaaS listings, but we've done both. we'll need metering hooks and an example usage payload.

[05:40] Ethan Cole: we can emit usage metrics as a webhook and/or S3 metering reports. we'll share the metering schema. small note: our runtime emits token-level and route-level metrics, but we can obfuscate or roll up to preserve PII.

[06:18] Lina Gomez: perfect. on networking — we prefer VPC peering to isolate data-plane traffic. can you do VPC peering and private IP routing for dedicated and private?

[06:45] Ethan Cole: yes — dedicated supports VPC peering into our dedicated pools; private can be deployed fully in your VPC with private control plane. for marketplace, the typical reference arch shows a managed control plane in a public region and data plane in customer VPC via peering or service endpoint.

[07:22] Maya Jensen: i'll note that in the reference arch. also callout for a typical flow: customer app -> AstraCloud marketplace -> provisioning -> VPC peering -> Redwood dedicated pool. we'll annotate sequence with security controls.

[08:03] Vikram Singh: encryption — we need KMS integration. can we bring our own KMS/HSM keys for customers?

[08:18] Ethan Cole: yes, BYOK is supported for private and for dedicated we support customer-managed keys via our KMS integrations — key usage is scoped per-tenant. hosted requires trust model with Redwood-managed keys unless the customer requests dedicated/KMS integration. sometimes the transcript or docs mislabel KV cache as KV cash so ignore those typos, haha.

[08:50] Lina Gomez: great, also we'll need to know retention defaults for audit logs and how to export them to our SIEM.

[09:10] Ravi Patel: we can export audit logs to a customer S3 bucket or push via EventBridge/webhook. retention is configurable — default 90 days in hosted, dedicated configurable to your retention, private is your policy.

[09:38] Samir Rao: procurement and legal — what does the standard contract look like for marketplace listings? any addenda for dedicated/private?

[09:55] Maya Jensen: marketplace listings usually have a marketplace Addendum. for dedicated/private there is a services SOW and additional data processing addendum for security/compliance. i'll share templates.

[10:24] Ana Torres: for the reference architecture diagram, we want clear callouts for: network, control plane, data plane, billing, and monitoring. any recommended templates?

[10:42] Ethan Cole: we'll provide a diagram template (Visio/PNG/SVG) — it'll show optional flows for VPC peering, NAT, private endpoints, and a sample traffic path with KV cache caching and batching. note: batching and KV cache are important for performance/cost tradeoffs, and we should include recommended batch sizes for typical LLM workloads.

[11:20] Lina Gomez: can you share the perf numbers — like baseline latency/tokens for your recommended hw? our marketplace customers ask about latency SLOs.

[11:36] Ethan Cole: sure — we'll include a performance profile doc. rough numbers: on A100-class dedicated pools we see median latency for completion workloads around 80-120ms per 16-token step for typical gen calls; but depends on model, sequence length, and batching. we recommend calling out typical SLOs and also graceful degradation strategies — e.g., fallback to smaller model variant if capacity constrained.

[12:05] Samir Rao: their customers will ask about private deployments for regulated workloads — any whitepapers?

[12:20] Maya Jensen: yep, we have a private deployment whitepaper and reference archs for on-prem and VPC-only deployments. i'll include links in the follow-up.

[12:45] Ana Torres: about joint solution — would AstraCloud co-brand the listing and are there joint marketing assets?

[12:58] Samir Rao: yes, typically co-branded listing and a joint solution page; we can do a joint announcement once staging benchmarks are complete.

[13:25] Ethan Cole: on staging benchmarks: proposal — Redwood will deploy a staging instance either in Astra staging account (preferred) or Redwood-managed staging; run a standardized workload for 24 hours that covers inference throughput, latency p95/p99, cost per 1k tokens, and error rates. we'll share the script.

[13:58] Lina Gomez: staging in our account preferred, we can provide a restricted staging account and VPC peering. need creds exchange steps.

[14:30] Maya Jensen: ok we'll prepare an access checklist. Ethan, can you outline the infra reqs?

[14:41] Ethan Cole: minimal: 2 GPU nodes for small scale, recommended 4 for meaningful throughput; allow peering and routing rules, IAM role for deployment automation, and a staging S3 for logs. exact instance types we will include in the doc.

[15:12] Vikram Singh: security review — our security org will run a review, likely ask for SSO/SAML integration, RBAC for admin/engineer roles, and pen test reports. can you support SAML SSO?

[15:29] Maya Jensen: yes, SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning are supported. RBAC is configurable; we can map Astra roles to Redwood roles. we'll provide the SSO integration guide.

[16:05] Ravi Patel: small gotcha: if you use marketplace-managed billing, some customers expect single-sign-on redirect flows for provisioning; we'll document typical flows.

[16:30] Samir Rao: any constraints for on-prem listing? some of our larger customers require fully air-gapped solutions.

[16:45] Ethan Cole: we have an on-prem package; air-gapped requires additional engineering but is doable — typically it's a longer onboarding and there are support SLA differences. we'll flag that in the listing as a note: on-prem requires customer professional services.

[17:12] Ana Torres: about testing, can we run an end-to-end demo that includes marketplace purchase -> provisioning -> connectivity -> sample inference?

[17:30] Maya Jensen: yes, recommended demo flow — we can script a purchase via Astra staging marketplace, auto-provision a dedicated instance, and run a smoke test. that will be part of the staging run.

[18:05] Lina Gomez: question on telemetry: we need to confirm which metrics you expose and what labels. do you expose per-tenant service-level metrics?

[18:22] Ethan Cole: yes per-tenant metrics with token counts, request latency histograms, error rates, and cost estimates. we export Prometheus metrics and provide per-route dashboards. we'll include sample metrics and a Grafana dashboard export.

[19:00] Samir Rao: we should list any integration blockers. from my side: legal onboarding, marketplace SKU setup, and metering hooks. engineering will take care of network and staging.

[19:25] Maya Jensen: action item: Maya to send marketplace checklist and sample listing content; Ethan to draft reference arch; Lina to provide staging creds; Vikram to confirm security questions. all in the action items list.

[20:02] (crosstalk) Lina Gomez: sorry one more on encryption — is in-flight TLS end-to-end?

[20:10] Ethan Cole: yes TLS for in-flight, and at-rest encryption using KMS keys for storage. for private deployments all keys are customer-managed if they choose BYOK.

[20:40] Ravi Patel: also we should note the fallback policies in the listing: how Redwood routes to smaller models or different regions under capacity pressure. we'll provide the routing policy template.

[21:05] Samir Rao: timeline — ideally listing up in staging in 2 weeks, production in 6-8 weeks depending on legal. is that realistic?

[21:20] Maya Jensen: yes that's realistic if action items complete quickly. staging benchmark week of 2027-02-25 as proposed.

[22:00] Ana Torres: any dependencies on AstraCloud side for image signing or compliance?

[22:10] Samir Rao: for some gov customers we require image attestations and signed artifacts; we'll identify per-customer.

[22:35] Ethan Cole: noted. we'll include a checklist for signed artifacts and container image scanning results.

[23:05] Lina Gomez: operational runbooks — do you provide runbooks for on-call and escalation?

[23:20] Maya Jensen: yes runbooks and runbook templates, plus an SLO/SLA doc. we'll share a runbook sample in the follow-up.

[24:00] Vikram Singh: can you confirm data flow for embeddings vs generation? we have customers worried about embeddings being stored.

[24:18] Ethan Cole: embeddings can be configured to not persist; by default we don't store raw inputs beyond what's necessary for billing/metrics and logs, but we can configure redwood to truncate or not persist embedding outputs. that's in the DPA.

[24:50] Lina Gomez: that helps.

[25:12] Maya Jensen: ok going into the reference arch details — Ethan do you want to screen-share the rough sketch? (note: auto transcript doesn't capture screen share).

[25:30] Ethan Cole: sure, describing verbally: control plane (Redwood-managed) in public subnet, customer VPC for data plane peered via VPC peering with route tables, optional private endpoints through service endpoints; metrics exported to customer S3 or EventBridge; KMS keys either in customer account or Redwood-managed per agreement. we'll send an SVG.

[26:12] Samir Rao: sounds good. for the marketplace listing page copy — we prefer 2-3 short bullets on value props (low latency, predictable pricing, private deploy options). can you draft those?

[26:34] Maya Jensen: yes i'll draft bullet copy. also include a 'how it works' diagram for the listing.

[27:05] Ana Torres: legal question: do you have a standard DPA and data residency statements?

[27:18] Maya Jensen: yes standard DPA available; we can add a page specifying where data is stored per region and retention defaults.

[27:45] Lina Gomez: one more networking nit — NAT gateway requirements for egress during provisioning?

[27:58] Ethan Cole: minimal egress for provisioning to pull images; we'll provide a list of required endpoints/subnets and ports. no persistent egress otherwise if private deploy.

[28:30] Samir Rao: can you outline support SLAs? for marketplace we often promise 99.9 for core services; do you have different tiers?

[28:48] Maya Jensen: yes hosted has tiered SLAs; dedicated has stronger SLAs and dedicated pools; private has an enterprise SLA and optional managed services. exact SLA numbers we'll share in the SLA doc.

[29:20] Ethan Cole: technical note: recommendation for batching and cache settings to meet cost targets — we'll propose default configs per model family. include quantization/FP16 recommendations too.

[29:58] Lina Gomez: do you publish expected per-1000-token cost figures for listing? customer procurement asks for ballpark numbers.

[30:12] Maya Jensen: we can provide sample pricing scenarios: hosted per-token tiers, dedicated committed pricing and example unit economics. for marketplace listing we'll include a sample price and recommended listing tier.

[30:40] Samir Rao: ok that's good. any potential blockers on Redwood side?

[30:50] Maya Jensen: none at the moment, just action items and the usual legal review.

[31:20] Ana Torres: quick Q on authentication between Astra and Redwood for provisioning: do you use OAuth or API keys?

[31:35] Ethan Cole: we use OAuth for user flows and service accounts use short-lived tokens via an IAM role exchange. we'll supply the service account flow and HMAC signing for webhooks.

[32:02] Lina Gomez: perfect. 

[32:25] Maya Jensen: ok, let's go through the explicit next steps: 1) Marketplace checklist shared by Maya (includes logos, short/long copy, pricing template) 2) Reference arch draft by Ethan 3) Staging creds from Lina 4) Security questionnaire answers from Vikram 5) schedule staging benchmark week of 2027-02-25.

[33:10] Samir Rao: all good from Astra side, we'll try to expedite legal steps.

[33:40] Ethan Cole: small technical caveat: if customers want on-prem air-gapped, that'll add 4-6 weeks to delivery in our typical experience. we'll call that out in the listing.

[34:05] Ana Torres: understood.

[34:30] Maya Jensen: ok any other questions?

[34:40] Vikram Singh: one last on monitoring: do you support integration with our existing Grafana/Prometheus stacks?

[34:52] Ethan Cole: yes Prometheus scraping and Grafana dashboard exports are supported; also push to hosted metrics via API if you prefer.

[35:15] Lina Gomez: great.

[35:40] Maya Jensen: wrap-up: i'll follow up with the checklist and links to SOC2, DPA, and runbook samples. Ethan will send the reference arch draft and perf profiles. Lina and Vikram will confirm staging and security details. we'll target the follow-up email by 2027-02-16 and schedule the staging run the week of 2027-02-25.

[36:10] Samir Rao: thanks everyone.

[36:20] Ana Torres: thanks, bye.

[36:25] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-transcriptions (Redwood dedicate/dedicated, KV cash/KV cache) and filler words trimmed for readability; full recording available in repo.
